name: repair_history
rows: Bronx Housing Justice Project -- case management export
Exported 2026-05-30 by Keisha Merriweather, intake paralegal

Tenant association reports the entrance door interlock still engages without a power-outage key; managing agent notified the same day by email and by telephone. Photographs from Apt 4A and from the lobby, taken on three separate dates, are in the intake folder together with the tenant association interest sheet.

Organizing meeting held in the lobby with tenants from 2B, 4A and 5C. Elevator outages and entrance security dominated the discussion; the January power dip and the March entrapment were both described from the floor. Eleven tenants signed the association interest sheet and two asked to be recorded as witnesses for any proceeding. Minutes circulated to the organizing staff.

Managing agent's correction confirmation letter of 2026-04-10 received and filed in the case record with the enclosure from our March letter. The roof-door closer repair described in the letter is shown closed in the HPD record. The letter was reviewed at the May association meeting, where tenants from 2B and 4A reported the entrance door had again failed to latch during the May 4 power dip; photographs were taken and added to the folder.

Walkthrough with the tenant of 3A: third-floor hallway plaster broken out above the cornice, missing apartment door viewer and repeated elevator outages recorded with dates and photographs. The out-of-date lobby postings were photographed as well. The owner's agent asked for a written complaint list before scheduling any visit.

Sent the owner's agent the compiled complaint list for 2323 Walton Avenue by certified mail with a request for a correction schedule and a walk-through date; the certified receipt is on file. No response has been received to date; a follow-up letter is drafted for the Litigation Director's signature.

Follow-up call with the tenant of 3A. Building-wide registration and posting items from the last inspection cycle remain outstanding and the elevator failed twice in April. The tenant has agreed to photograph the hallway conditions weekly and to collect names of neighbors willing to join an association drive if the building is selected.

Met the tenant of 1A at the building and walked the basement, the rear yard and the compactor room. Compactor room odor and a broken rear-yard fence reported to the managing agent the same day; the superintendent made temporary repairs the same week and re-set the fence posts.

Rear-yard fence repaired and photographed for the file. Compactor odor returns in warm weather exactly as the tenant of 1A described in his April letter; asked the superintendent for the compactor cleaning log and for the name of the hauling contractor. Neither has been provided.

Intake call with two additional Bolton Street households confirmed the compactor odor and a basement corridor lighting outage near the meter room; both households added to the complaint list and asked to keep a written record of dates. The superintendent's channel remains open and he has confirmed receipt of the lighting report.

Tenant of 2C reports a persistent bathroom ceiling leak that began during the January boiler shutdown, when the building was without heat for four days. The owner's agent sent a plumber once in February; the leak returned within two weeks and the ceiling stain has spread from the light fixture toward the corner. Photographs from January and February are in the intake folder.

Second plumber visit logged by the managing agent; the work order describes a drain-line snaking above the bathroom. The tenant reports the ceiling stain has widened since February and filed current photographs. Heat has held since the January shutdown, though the hallway outside 2C stays cold and the tenant has asked about weather-stripping.

Tenant of 2C reports the bathroom leak is active again after the second plumber visit; the stain now reaches the corner of the room and the plaster is soft to the touch. Asked the managing agent for a written repair schedule and for the name of the contractor who will open the ceiling; if nothing arrives this month the file goes to the litigation team ahead of the July calendar date.
